What is the equation of the ellipse given below?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13958359/assets/b6eb2c0222181eaa4eb2a1c232fdf2eee905ab0e0a8a9c2284911ab8dd26cade.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\dfrac{(x-h)^2}{{a}^2}+\dfrac{(y-k)^2}{{b}^2}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(-1,-3),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=2,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=4.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-(-1))^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-3))^{2}}{{4}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{16} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(1,-3),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=4,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=2.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-3))^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
